per_view.notes: Slender grey tube with a distinct front upper-deck hump blending within the front third, plus a consistent main-deck window band and hump windows. Tall swept vertical fin and a thin horizontal stabilizer at rear. Engines are bunched together near the wing root/mid-fuselage rather than four spread underwing nacelles; count unclear. Nose gear plus a few clustered wheels. Uniform grey livery, no whit

Slender grey tube, dashed main-deck window line plus a separate window row on a short front hump. Tail has a tall swept dark fin but no clear horizontal stabilizer. Engines read as a jumbled cluster under the wing, hard to count four; a few small wheels sit under them and one near the rear. Nose end is fairly blunt.

Head-on: four dark nacelles, two per wing under swept wings, plausible spacing. Rounded grey fuselage with a small raised cockpit hump and dark windshield. Wings nearly flat, minimal visible dihedral. Thin vertical fin at top; horizontal stabilizers not visible. Nose gear plus main-gear wheels present. Coherent grey livery, clean assembly. No fuselage window line visible from front.

Head-on view: circular fuselage cross-section, four underwing nacelles on pylons with plausible spacing, tall vertical fin. No horizontal stabilizers visible at the tail. Several main-gear bogies below the belly. Uniform grey, no windows/doors, no accents. Wings show slight sweep/dihedral. Clean assembly, no floating parts.

Top-down: four nacelles, two per swept tapering wing, offset ahead of leading edge, good spacing. Fuselage is a thick cylindrical tube with dashed window/door lines and a dark cockpit rectangle at nose; an oval outline hints at upper deck but hump extent unreadable from top. Swept horizontal stabilizers present; vertical fin edge-on. Coherent grey/light livery, clean assembly, no floating parts.

Slender grey tube with no upper-deck hump and a flat blunt nose cap. Four engine shapes: two under the wing on pylons, two awkwardly attached near the rear fuselage/tail. Swept tapering wings, tall swept fin. A passenger window dash-line runs the fuselage. Only a tiny nose-gear stub; no main trucks. Monochrome grey, no accent. Without a hump it reads as a generic four-jet, not a 747.

Slender light-grey tube with a partial front hump and a dashed window line. Swept tapering wings with dihedral and a tail fin plus horizontal stabilizers. Engine nacelles and dark gear clusters appear near the wing root but are hard to resolve as four cleanly spaced underslung units. Tail end is a blunt flat cylinder lacking a tapered tail cone; some parts read as clustered.

Slender grey tube with blunt flat-ended nose (no taper) and no upper-deck hump. Swept vertical fin plus horizontal stabilizers read well. Engine nacelles are bunched together beneath the mid-belly rather than spread on wing pylons; wings themselves are barely visible. Nose-gear strut and a main-gear wheel cluster present. Dotted window line along fuselage. Coherent monochrome grey.

Upper deck is a separate smaller cylinder telescoped into the fuselage front with a flat blunt nose cap and visible seam/gap, reading as floating stacked tubes rather than a faired hump. Swept dihedral wings, tall fin, and ~4 underwing nacelles present. Window rows on both lobes. All flat grey, no white livery.

critic.fix_suggestion: Improve 'Partial-length upper-deck hump' (mean 4.43/10). Target the 8 anchor: distinct partial-length upper deck starting at the nose and blending down within roughly the front third of the fuselage; then the 10 anchor: iconic 747 hump: starts at the cockpit, smoothly faired into the crown, ends around one-third of the length, with a visible cockpit region on the upper lobe.
